title: Tool version history and rollback
why: Every save overwrites the single `tools` row (`database.upsert` ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE). A bad edit from a second tab, an LLM via `omniforge_create_tool`, or a mis-paste is unrecoverable; the content-hash `revision` exists only to detect conflicts, not to recover.
what: Add a `tool_versions` table written on every upsert (revision hash, code, schema, requirements, author/client, timestamp). Studio gets a History panel with diff and one-click Restore, which creates a new version rather than rewriting history.

title: Input-schema editor in the dashboard
why: The dashboard cannot create or edit `inputSchema`: `save()` reuses the existing schema or `{}` for new tools, and the UI says 'Create or change schemas through MCP'. So every tool authored in the browser is parameterless; a lottery fetcher cannot take a draw date unless an LLM created it.
what: Add a schema builder (name/type/required/description rows) that emits Draft 2020-12, with an 'infer from sample JSON' button and a raw-JSON advanced mode using the existing `validate_schema`.

title: Export / import tool bundles
why: Tools live only inside one SQLite file in a named Docker volume. There is no way to move a tool to another instance, share it, or keep a copy outside the container.
what: `GET /api/tools/{name}/export` and `GET /api/export` emit a JSON bundle (metadata, code, schema, requirements, versions). `POST /api/import` accepts a bundle with rename/skip/overwrite strategy and reuses `ToolIn` validation.

title: Git sync: tools as files
why: Code review, blame, branching and backup all want files, not BLOBs. The README's 'self-updating' vision has no path for updating *tools*, only the image.
what: Optional `OMNIFORGE_TOOLS_DIR`: each tool materialises as `tools/<name>/main.py|main.js` + `tool.json`. DB stays the index; a watcher imports changes and a Git remote can be pushed/pulled from the dashboard or CLI.

title: Per-tool secrets vault
why: Scripts need API keys (lottery API, Pushover, Xero). Today the only options are hard-coding them in `code` (stored plaintext, visible to every dashboard visitor) or container env vars, which `runner.run_tool` copies wholesale into *every* script.
what: Add a `secrets` table encrypted with a master key from env/keyfile; write-only in the UI; injected as env vars only into the owning tool's subprocess after the environment is scrubbed; values redacted from stdout/stderr like `_safe_stderr` already does for installer output.

title: Run history and logs
why: Run results exist only in the browser tab (`outputSnapshot`) and MCP responses. When LibreChat reports a tool failed, there is nothing on the server to look at; `stderr` is lost.
what: Persist each run (tool, revision, origin: dashboard/MCP/key id, argument hash, duration, exit code, timed_out, bounded stdout/stderr). Add a Runs page and a per-tool recent-runs list in the studio with retention settings.

title: Scheduled runs (cron)
why: A bonus-ball fetcher is naturally 'run every Wednesday and Saturday evening'; today only an LLM or a human can trigger it.
what: Per-tool cron expression and fixed arguments; an in-process scheduler (APScheduler or a simple asyncio loop) with jitter and missed-run policy; results land in run history and optionally a notification tool.

title: Webhook triggers
why: n8n, GitHub, Home Assistant and cron-on-another-box cannot call a tool without speaking JSON-RPC and holding the global Bearer key.
what: `POST /hooks/{tool}/{hook-token}` with body-as-arguments, per-tool tokens, schema validation and the same run pipeline; responses can be sync or `202` with a run id.

title: Output schemas and saved test cases
why: Tools are tested by eyeballing stdout once. There is no way to re-check a tool after editing it, and MCP clients get untyped text even when the tool prints JSON.
what: Optional `outputSchema` (MCP 2025-06-18) validated against parsed stdout; per-tool saved test cases (arguments + expected JSON/status) with a 'Run all tests' button and a CLI/CI hook.

title: MCP prompts and resources
why: Only `tools/*` exists; `resources/list` and `prompts/list` return -32601. Clients like Claude and LibreChat can surface prompts and resources, which is how you give a model usage guidance and reference data without a tool call.
what: Store prompt templates and static/derived resources (tool documentation, latest run output, uploaded reference files) and expose `prompts/list|get`, `resources/list|read|templates/list` with change notifications.

title: Template gallery and shareable packs
why: Four examples exist (two greetings, `requests.Request` that does not even send, lodash sort). None resembles a real job such as fetching a web page, calling an authenticated API or returning a table.
what: Ship 10-15 curated templates with schemas and secrets placeholders (HTTP fetch + parse, authenticated JSON API, CSV summary, notification, scrape-and-extract like the bonus-ball tool). Allow installing packs from a Git URL or bundle (F-03), with a clear 'community, unreviewed' label.

title: Additional runtimes: shell and TypeScript
why: Many 'tools' are one-line shell pipelines; TypeScript is what most Node authors write. `_runtime` hard-codes python and node.
what: Add `bash` (no package manager) and `typescript` via Node 22's `--experimental-strip-types` (no build step). Keep the runtime table data-driven so `validate_requirements` and the runner share one registry.

title: Lightweight multi-user and attribution
why: Even a household/small team shares one unauthenticated dashboard; nothing records who changed what. Full RBAC is overkill for a self-hosted single-container product.
what: Users table with roles (admin, author, viewer) layered on R-01; author stored on versions and runs; tools can be marked read-only to non-owners.

title: Usage and latency observability
why: Overview shows only saved/enabled counts; nobody can answer 'which tools does LibreChat actually call, how often do they fail, and how slow is the install path?'.
what: Aggregate run history into per-tool and per-client counters (calls, errors, p50/p95 duration, install time); show on Overview and per-tool; expose `/metrics` (A-06).

title: Quotas and concurrency limits
why: A looping LLM can call a tool hundreds of times; each call is a fresh subprocess with no cap on concurrency, CPU time per minute or daily calls.
what: Global max concurrent runs (semaphore), per-key calls/minute, per-tool daily call cap and total runtime budget; over-quota returns an `isError` result with a plain reason.

title: Tool annotations and titles
why: MCP clients use `title` and `annotations` (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) to decide when to ask the user for confirmation. OmniForge sends only name/description/inputSchema.
what: Add optional `title` and four annotation checkboxes in the studio; include them in `tools/list`.

title: Tags and groups for the library
why: The list is flat and sorted by `updated_at`; search is substring over name+description. With 30+ tools, 'all my lottery tools' or 'everything that needs a secret' is not findable.
what: Free-form tags stored in metadata, tag filter chips alongside the state/runtime filter, and optional tag-scoped exposure per API key (F-20).

title: Shared helper modules
why: Tools that call the same API duplicate auth/parsing code; there is no way to `import` a shared module because each run is a single file in a scratch directory.
what: A 'library' tool kind whose files are copied/bound into the run directory (`omniforge_lib/`) and on `PYTHONPATH`/`NODE_PATH`; versioned like tools.

title: Dependency cache management
why: `ensure_dependencies` creates a new hashed environment per requirements change and the README says old caches 'remain until an administrator removes them'; incomplete directories raise 'administrator review required' with no UI to review.
what: A Packages page listing cached environments per tool (size, requirements, last used, complete/incomplete), with prune, rebuild and 'clear incomplete' actions.

title: Per-client tool visibility
why: Every client with the one Bearer key sees every enabled tool. David wants some tools for LibreChat only, or a read-only subset for a phone client.
what: With named keys (R-02), allow a per-key allowlist (tool names or tags); `tools/list` and `tools/call` are filtered by the authenticated key.

title: Dashboard and management-API authentication
why: `/`, `/api/tools*`, `/api/config` and `/api/tools/{name}/run` have no auth at all: anyone on the LAN can read every script (including embedded credentials), edit, delete or execute code in the container.
what: Admin password set on first boot (setup screen) or env; signed session cookie with SameSite=Strict + CSRF token; the same session gates the dashboard and `/api/*`. Keep an env escape hatch for trusted-LAN dev.

title: Named per-client API keys with scopes
why: `_check_api_key` compares one shared `OMNIFORGE_API_KEY`; it cannot be rotated without recreating the container, cannot be revoked per client, and gives LibreChat the same rights as a throwaway test client (including `omniforge_create_tool`).
what: `api_keys` table (hashed), create/revoke in the dashboard, shown once; scopes `tools:call`, `tools:author`, `admin`; key id recorded on runs and audit rows. Keep env key as a bootstrap option.

title: OAuth 2.1 resource server for hosted MCP clients
why: Claude.ai custom connectors and other hosted MCP clients require OAuth (authorization-server discovery via RFC 9728/8414, dynamic client registration) and cannot send a static Bearer header. Today OmniForge is reachable only from clients that allow custom headers.
what: Implement the MCP 2025-06-18 resource-server role: `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, bearer JWT validation against a configurable external authorization server (Authentik/Keycloak/Auth0), scope mapping to R-02 scopes. Do not build an authorization server.

title: Scrub the subprocess environment
why: Verified on a local instance: a tool containing `print(os.environ)` returns `OMNIFORGE_API_KEY` and all paths. `run_tool` does `os.environ.copy()`; only installer children get a minimal env.
what: Give script children the same minimal environment as installers (`PATH`, `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `LANG`) plus `PYTHONPATH`/`NODE_PATH` and tool-specific secrets (F-05). Regression test that the key is absent.

title: Real per-run isolation (tiered plan)
why: Scripts run as the app user with the app's filesystem, network and DB. One careless `shutil.rmtree` or a malicious dependency owns the instance. The original brief asked for per-run isolation; the no-Docker-socket stance rules out container-per-run from inside the container.
what: Tier 1 (ship first): bubblewrap in-image: `bwrap --unshare-all [--share-net] --ro-bind` runtime+deps, tmpfs `/tmp`, per-run work dir, `--die-with-parent`, seccomp; requires unprivileged user namespaces on the host (common on Unraid/Debian, document the `--security-opt` fallback). Tier 2: nsjail for cgroup CPU/mem/pids limits. Tier 3: gVisor `runsc` as the container runtime (host-level change, keeps no-socket stance). Firecracker/container-per-run rejected as too heavy for one container. Per-tool 'network: on/off' flag.

title: Process-tree termination and rlimits
why: `subprocess.run(timeout=)` kills only the direct child; a tool that spawns `node`/`curl` leaves orphans running after timeout (documented as unimplemented). `OMNIFORGE_MAX_SCRIPT_MEMORY_MB` is 'declared only'.
what: Start children with `start_new_session=True`, kill the process group on timeout; `preexec_fn` sets `RLIMIT_AS`, `RLIMIT_NPROC`, `RLIMIT_FSIZE`, `RLIMIT_CPU`; make the memory setting real.

title: Bounded stdout/stderr
why: Verified: a tool printing 5 MB returns 5 MB through `/api/tools/{name}/run` and would do the same via MCP, which LLM clients then try to put in context. `capture_output=True` is unbounded in memory.
what: Stream child output to files or a bounded reader, cap at a configurable 256 KiB-1 MiB per stream, append a `[truncated N bytes]` marker and `truncated: true` in the result.

title: Non-blocking execution and a concurrency limit
why: `api_run_tool` and `mcp_endpoint` are `async def` but call the blocking `run_tool` (and `ensure_dependencies`, up to 120 s + 125 s lock wait) directly, so the single uvicorn event loop freezes: while one tool runs, the dashboard, `tools/list` and every other client stall.
what: Run the subprocess with `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` (or `run_in_threadpool`) under a global semaphore; installs likewise; add a 503/`isError` 'busy' response when the semaphore is saturated.

title: MCP Streamable HTTP compliance
why: Verified: `notifications/initialized` gets a JSON-RPC error with `id: null` (spec: HTTP 202, no body); batch arrays return a FastAPI 422; `initialize` echoes any `protocolVersion` string back; no `Mcp-Session-Id`, no `MCP-Protocol-Version` header handling, no `Accept` negotiation, no Origin check (DNS-rebinding risk for a LAN service); `GET /mcp` returns a made-up `initial-connections` event; `tools/list` ignores `cursor`; `listChanged: false` so clients never learn about new tools. The official `mcp` package is already in `requirements.txt` and unused.
what: Replace the handwritten transport with the SDK's Streamable HTTP server (sessions, SSE for server-to-client notifications, protocol negotiation 2024-11-05/2025-03-26/2025-06-18), send `notifications/tools/list_changed` on save/toggle/delete, validate Origin, implement cursor pagination, return 405 for unsupported GET when SSE is disabled.

title: Structured tool results
why: Every result is one text block; the dashboard already detects JSON stdout for pretty-printing but MCP clients get a string they must re-parse. Spec 2025-06-18 defines `structuredContent` + `outputSchema`.
what: If stdout parses as a JSON object, return it in `structuredContent` alongside the text block; expose `outputSchema` when the tool declares one (F-09); keep `isError` semantics.

title: Audit trail
why: Nothing records that an LLM created `foo` via `omniforge_create_tool` at 02:14, or that a tool was deleted. `updated_at` is the only trace and it is overwritten.
what: Append-only `audit` table: actor (session/key id), action (create/update/delete/toggle/run/install/key-rotate/import), target, revision before/after, remote address, timestamp; viewable and exportable from the dashboard.

title: Backup and restore
why: All state is `omniforge.db` plus `lib/` caches in Docker volumes; no documented backup, no consistent-snapshot mechanism (a file copy of a live SQLite DB can be torn), and no restore path.
what: `GET /api/admin/backup` using SQLite's online backup/`VACUUM INTO`, scheduled backups to a mounted path with retention, `POST /api/admin/restore`, WAL mode, and a README runbook (caches are rebuildable, DB is not).

title: HTTPS / secure context story
why: PWA install and service workers need a secure context, so the Help page tells LAN users they probably cannot install. Hosted MCP clients also require HTTPS. The Connect page derives the endpoint from `location.origin`, which is wrong behind a reverse proxy without forwarded headers.
what: Document and ship a Caddy/Traefik example (LAN TLS via internal CA or Tailscale cert), run uvicorn with `--proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips`, honour `X-Forwarded-Proto/Host` in `/api/config`, optional built-in TLS (`OMNIFORGE_TLS_CERT/KEY`).

title: Upgrade and migration framework
why: `_ensure_schema` only does `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`; there is no schema version, so every feature above that adds a column risks breaking older DBs. Version is hard-coded `0.1.0`; the 'self-updating' goal has no update check.
what: `schema_version` table with ordered idempotent migrations run at startup under a lock; `/api/version` with app version + image build SHA; dashboard 'update available' check against the Docker Hub tag list; CHANGELOG and semver image tags.

title: Supply-chain controls for installs
why: Installs pull from PyPI/npm by name with optional exact version; unpinned names freeze at whatever resolved first. No hash verification, no allow/deny list, no audit, `--no-audit` is passed to npm, and install logs are deleted after success.
what: Per-tool lockfile generated on first install (pip `--require-hashes` from `pip-compile --generate-hashes`; npm `package-lock.json` integrity), an admin package allow/deny list, optional private index/mirror env, retained install logs, and an advisory scan (`pip-audit`, `npm audit`) surfaced in F-19.

title: Rate limiting
why: No limiter on `/mcp`, `/api/tools/{name}/run` or (future) login; `slowapi` is in `requirements.txt` but never imported.
what: Token-bucket limits per key/IP on `tools/call`, `/run`, install-triggering runs and login; `429` with `Retry-After`; defaults generous for a single user.

title: Per-tool resource limits
why: Timeout is global (`OMNIFORGE_MAX_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS` + an undocumented 15 s), memory is unenforced, and a scraper that legitimately needs 90 s shares settings with a 50 ms formatter.
what: Per-tool overrides for timeout, memory, CPU seconds, output cap and network access, bounded by admin maximums; shown in the studio's advanced section and enforced via R-06/R-05.

title: Health and readiness endpoints
why: No `/healthz`; the Dockerfile has no `HEALTHCHECK`, so Unraid/compose cannot tell a wedged event loop (see R-08) from a healthy one.
what: `GET /healthz` (process up) and `GET /readyz` (DB readable, lib root writable, python/node present); `HEALTHCHECK` in the Dockerfile; uptime and version in the response.

title: CI gating and release pipeline
why: `dockerhub.yml` pushes `:latest` on every push to `main` with no test dependency; `test.yml` runs only on PRs and non-main branches. Compose references `ionic-developer/omniforge:latest` while CI pushes `dbzocchi/omniforge:latest`. Only amd64 is built.
what: Make the publish job `needs: test`; run tests on `main` too; tag images with semver + git SHA plus `latest`; build `linux/amd64,linux/arm64`; attach SBOM/provenance; ship a pull-only `docker-compose.yml` for users and a `compose.dev.yml` for building.

title: Supported Node runtime
why: The Dockerfile installs `nodejs npm` from Debian bookworm apt, which is Node 18 (end-of-life since April 2025) and an old npm; many current packages require Node 20+.
what: Install Node 22 LTS from the official tarball or NodeSource with a pinned version and checksum; print runtime versions on `/api/config` and in the studio's runtime selector.

title: Multi-worker and multi-process safety
why: `Database._cache` is per process with a 5 s TTL and `threading.Lock`; the design doc already warns another worker's stale cache could serve old code. `uvicorn --workers 2` would silently break hot reload for up to 5 s and double the install lock contention.
what: Either document single-worker as a hard constraint and refuse to start with `--workers>1`, or drive invalidation off SQLite `PRAGMA data_version` so caches are coherent across processes.

title: Install-path hardening
why: The installer runs with full network as the app UID into a volume the app also reads; there is no size quota on `OMNIFORGE_LIB_ROOT`, and concurrent installs for different tools can all run at once (each up to 120 s).
what: Global install semaphore, per-volume size quota with a clear error, optional egress restriction to the registry hosts once R-05 exists, and installs recorded in run history/audit.

title: Adopt the official `mcp` SDK server
why: `requirements.txt` installs `mcp`, `sse-starlette`, `slowapi` and `pydantic-settings`, none imported; `_handle_rpc` reimplements four methods by hand and will keep diverging from the spec.
what: Mount the SDK's Streamable HTTP ASGI app at `/mcp` and register tools dynamically from the DB on each list/call (hot reload preserved); keep the built-ins as SDK tools. This is the implementation vehicle for R-09/R-10/F-10.

title: Remove dead configuration and reconcile names
why: `OMNIFORGE_RUNTIME_IMAGE`, `OMNIFORGE_SCRIPT_HOST` and the `omniforge_scripts` volume are leftovers from the Docker-per-run era (README calls one 'historical'); `lifespan` is a no-op with a misleading comment; compose and CI disagree on the image name.
what: Delete the unused env vars, volume, dependencies and comment; one canonical image name; `.env.example` matching the real variable set.

title: Per-run working directory
why: `run_tool` writes `SCRATCH_ROOT/{tool.id}.py` and runs with `cwd=SCRATCH_ROOT` shared by all tools: two concurrent runs of one tool rewrite the same file (a save mid-run can execute mixed code), and any tool can read every other tool's source from the shared directory.
what: `tempfile.mkdtemp` per run (deleted afterwards unless 'keep for debugging' is on), code written there, `cwd` set to it; this is also the mount point for R-05.

title: Schema integrity: UNIQUE name, WAL, busy timeout
why: `tools.name` has only a non-unique index; uniqueness is enforced by a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` check, and legacy duplicates are tolerated 'without migration'. `sqlite3.connect` uses defaults (no WAL, 5 s busy timeout) so a long write can throw 'database is locked'.
what: Migration (R-14) that renames legacy duplicates to `name__dupN`, adds `UNIQUE(name)`, enables WAL and sets `busy_timeout`; keep the transactional guard as belt and braces.

title: JSON-RPC envelope correctness
why: Non-object bodies and arrays produce FastAPI 422 `detail` payloads instead of JSON-RPC `-32700/-32600`; `jsonrpc` field is never checked; errors use `id: null` even when the request id was known; unauthorized returns a 401 JSON-RPC body that the spec says should be a plain 401 with `WWW-Authenticate`.
what: Accept raw body, parse manually, emit spec-shaped errors, echo ids, add `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` on 401. Mostly subsumed by I-01 if the SDK is adopted.

title: Split the 50 KB single-file dashboard
why: `dashboard.html` is 574 lines with all JS inline; CI extracts the `<script>` by string-splitting to lint it, and `tests/dashboard_ui.cjs` hand-rolls a 300-line fake DOM. Every feature above lands in this one file.
what: Move JS to `/assets/app.js` (ES module, still no build step) with small modules (api, router, editor, library, connect); serve via the existing allowlist and precache; replace the fake DOM with jsdom or rely on Playwright for behaviour.

title: Honest timeout semantics
why: The effective limit is `MAX_TIMEOUT_MS/1000 + 15` seconds, documented as 'currently adds 15 seconds' with no rationale; the error text reports the configured value, not the enforced one; `timed_out` is detected via exit code 124, which a script could itself return.
what: Enforce exactly the configured (or per-tool, R-17) timeout, track timeouts via the exception, report `timed_out` structurally in MCP results, and start the clock only after dependency preparation (already the case) but report both durations.

title: Test-strategy gaps
why: Tests are strong on dashboard races and dependency caching but there is no test for: secrets leaking into scripts (they do), process-tree kill, output caps, event-loop blocking under concurrent requests, MCP transport conformance with a real client, or backup/restore.
what: Add an MCP conformance suite using the official Python client over Streamable HTTP; a secret-leak regression; a 'spawn child then timeout' test; an output-cap test; an asyncio concurrency test (list while a 3 s tool runs); make Playwright runs non-optional in CI on `main`.

title: Structured server logging
why: Only uvicorn access logs exist; tool failures, install failures and conflicts are returned to the caller and otherwise vanish.
what: JSON logs with request id, actor, tool, revision, duration, exit status; `OMNIFORGE_LOG_LEVEL`; correlate with run history ids.

title: Redact secrets from script output
why: `_safe_stderr` redacts env values only for installer output; script stdout/stderr (including tracebacks that print local variables) is returned verbatim.
what: Apply the same bounded redaction of known secret values (vault entries, keys) to script stdout/stderr before storing or returning them.

title: Protocol version negotiation
why: `initialize` returns whatever `protocolVersion` the client sent, including an empty string, and advertises `listChanged: false`.
what: Negotiate from a supported list (2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18), reject unknown versions per spec, advertise real capabilities. Subsumed by I-01.

title: Dependency environment reuse across tools
why: Caches are keyed by tool id *and* requirements hash, so ten tools that all need `requests==2.32.5` install it ten times and consume ten copies of disk.
what: Key environments by `(language, requirements-hash)` only, with a per-tool reference map for pruning (F-19); migrate existing per-tool directories lazily.

title: Failed-run explainer
why: A failed test shows raw stdout/stderr in a `<pre>` plus 'Failed · exit 1 · 99 ms'. A newcomer sees a Python traceback with a scratch path like `/tmp/omniforge/46c2b4.py` and no link back to their code.
what: Parse tracebacks/stack traces, map the scratch path to 'your script', highlight the failing line in the editor, show the exact stdin JSON that was sent, and offer a one-line plain-English summary ('Line 3: divided by zero - `d` was missing from inputs').

title: Input form generated from the schema
why: Test inputs are a raw JSON textarea defaulting to `{}`; a user whose tool needs `{"draw_date":"2026-10-15"}` has to know JSON syntax and the schema (shown read-only further up).
what: Render fields from `properties` (type-aware controls, required markers, descriptions) with 'Edit as JSON' toggle; reuse the same renderer for webhook/cron argument entry.

title: 'What is MCP?' explainer with a diagram
why: Help says 'Think of a tool as a named script your AI can ask the server to run', then jumps to JSON-RPC methods. The Connect page talks about `initialize`, `tools/list`, Streamable HTTP and SSE stubs.
what: A short illustrated page: Your AI app -> OmniForge -> your script -> answer; three roles (client, server, tool); a glossary (endpoint, key, schema, enable); and 'you never need to send JSON-RPC yourself'. Move protocol detail under 'Advanced'.

title: Per-client connection recipes
why: Connect shows one generic HTTP request template. LibreChat needs a `librechat.yaml` `mcpServers` block with `type: streamable-http` and a headers map; Claude Code needs `claude mcp add --transport http ... --header`; Claude Desktop needs `mcp-remote`; n8n needs its MCP Client node settings.
what: A client picker (LibreChat, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Claude.ai connector, Cursor, n8n, curl) emitting a copyable snippet with the real origin and a `<YOUR_API_KEY>` placeholder, plus per-client caveats (HTTPS/OAuth required, header support).

title: Connection self-test and last-seen clients
why: Connect says 'Connected clients: Not tracked'. After following the instructions, the user cannot tell whether LibreChat ever reached the server.
what: A 'Test from this browser' button that performs initialize + tools/list through the real endpoint with the user's key, and a last-seen list (key name, client `name/version` from `initialize`, last call, tool count) fed by run history.

title: Real code editor
why: The editor is a `<textarea>` with a line-number gutter and Tab handling; no syntax highlighting, bracket matching, search or error squiggles - painful for anything beyond ten lines.
what: Vendor CodeMirror 6 (no CDN, matches the self-hosted stance) with Python/JS modes, keep the textarea as a fallback and the existing keyboard/escape behaviour and dirty tracking.

title: Richer library rows
why: Rows show name, description, runtime and an Enabled toggle. Nothing says whether a tool has ever run, when, whether it failed, or whether it takes inputs.
what: Add last-run status/time, call count, 'needs inputs' and 'needs secrets' badges, and sort options (name, last run, most called).

title: Streaming install and run progress
why: First run of a tool with packages shows a static 'Preparing dependencies... up to 120 seconds' message while the whole server is blocked (R-08); the user has no idea whether pip is downloading or hung.
what: Server-sent progress events for install (resolved package list, download/complete) and run (started, stdout chunks, finished) rendered live in the output pane; resolved versions shown after install.

title: Save & Test in one action
why: Testing requires Save first; the Run button is disabled while dirty with the title 'Save changes before testing'. The edit-save-run loop costs two clicks and a status message every iteration.
what: A 'Save & Test' primary action (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter) that saves then runs the saved revision, preserving the dirty-state model and 412 handling.

title: Duplicate a tool
why: Making a variant means opening a tool, copying the code, creating a new tool and re-entering requirements/schema by hand.
what: 'Make a copy' in the studio that opens a new draft with `name_copy`, same code, requirements, schema and annotations.

title: 'How your AI sees this tool' preview
why: Users write descriptions without knowing they are the model's only guide to when to call the tool; the exact `tools/list` entry is invisible.
what: A preview card showing the tool entry as clients receive it (name, title, description, schema rendered as a parameter table, annotations) with guidance on writing descriptions that help the model.

title: Pending-action and busy feedback
why: While a run or install is in flight, `busy` disables all buttons but the only cue is 'Working... Keep this tab open'; there is no cancel.
what: A visible progress indicator with elapsed time, a Cancel button that kills the run (R-06), and a clear 'server busy' state when the concurrency limit (R-08) is hit.

title: Guided 'new tool' wizard
why: David's words: users have 'never seen anything like this'. The studio presents name, runtime, description, a blank script, folded packages and a JSON textarea all at once.
what: Five-step wizard: What should it do? -> Which inputs (name/type, plain words)? -> Python or Node (with 'not sure: Python')? -> generated skeleton (reads inputs, prints JSON) -> Test -> Connect. Each step writes into the normal studio so nothing is hidden afterwards.

title: Plain-language error catalogue
why: Errors are accurate but technical: 'Dependency installation failed; script was not run: <pip tail>', 'Arguments do not match inputSchema', 'Tool changed in another tab or client; reload before testing it'.
what: Map known failure classes to a short explanation + next step ('`reqests` is not on PyPI - did you mean `requests`?', 'Your AI sent `date` but the tool expects `draw_date`'), keep the technical detail behind 'Show details'.

title: Secure-by-default first boot
why: Leaving `OMNIFORGE_API_KEY` empty disables MCP auth entirely, the dashboard is open, and the Overview tells users to rely on a trusted network. Newcomers will deploy with the defaults.
what: On first boot with no admin configured, show a setup screen that sets the admin password and generates the first MCP key (shown once); auth on by default; timeout and output caps on; per-tool network off once R-05 exists.

title: Realistic one-click examples
why: The 'requests' example deliberately 'does not send a network request' and the lodash example sorts four numbers. Neither shows how to accept an input, call a real URL, use a secret or return a table.
what: Replace/extend with: 'Fetch a page and extract a number' (bonus-ball style), 'Call a JSON API with a secret', 'Summarise a CSV from a URL', 'Send a Pushover/Telegram message'; each with schema, sample inputs and expected output.

title: 'Connect to Claude / LibreChat' helpers with a readiness checklist
why: The Connect page is one-size-fits-all and lists limitations rather than checking them; a beginner cannot tell whether the blocker is HTTPS, a missing key or a disabled tool.
what: Buttons per client (U-04) plus a live checklist: server reachable at this origin, HTTPS yes/no, key configured, at least one tool enabled, client has called `initialize` (U-05); a QR code for phone clients.

title: 'Ask your AI to build it' flow
why: `omniforge_instructions` + `omniforge_create_tool` already let an LLM author tools, but the dashboard never tells beginners this exists or how to phrase the request.
what: A 'Build it with your AI' panel: copyable prompt ('Using OmniForge, create a tool that ...'), explanation that the AI will save but not run it, and in the library a 'Created by <client>' badge and a 'Review before enabling' option (new MCP-created tools default to disabled).

title: Live onboarding checklist on Overview
why: Overview shows a static 'create/test/connect' story and counts. It cannot show progress because the server does not know whether a tool was ever tested or called.
what: Tick list driven by real state: first tool saved, first successful test, key created, first external `tools/list`, first external `tools/call`; each links to the right screen.

title: CLI and API tokens
why: The management API is unauthenticated REST meant for the browser; scripting it means hand-rolling `curl` with `If-Match` headers.
what: A small `omniforge` CLI (pip-installable, single file) using R-02 tokens: `login`, `list`, `pull/push <name>`, `run <name> --args`, `logs`, `export/import`; JSON output for scripting.

title: Git-backed tools repo with CI
why: Advanced users want pull requests, review and automatic deployment of tools, mirroring how the image itself is built.
what: Repo layout from F-04, `omniforge validate` (schema, requirements, syntax) as a GitHub Action, deploy-on-merge via the CLI/API, and a `POST /api/git/pull` webhook to sync a configured remote.

title: Environment promotion (dev -> prod)
why: David tests on a scratch instance and runs production at 192.168.0.180; there is no way to move an exact revision between them.
what: Bundles carry revision hashes; `omniforge promote <name> --to prod` imports a pinned revision; instances show an environment label and colour in the top bar.

title: Typed schemas from code
why: Authors must hand-write JSON Schema (or cannot, in the browser). The code already defines the inputs it reads.
what: Convention: Python `def main(draw_date: str, count: int = 1) -> dict` with a docstring, or a `SCHEMA = {...}` constant; Node JSDoc/`module.exports.schema`. On save, parse and generate `inputSchema`/`outputSchema`; the studio shows the derived schema and lets the author override.

title: Prompts and resources authoring UI
why: F-10 adds the protocol primitives; advanced users need to author prompt templates with arguments and bind resources (files, run outputs) without editing the DB.
what: Prompt and Resource kinds in the library with their own studio forms, argument schemas, and preview of `prompts/get` output.

title: Metrics endpoint and tracing
why: No `/metrics`; Prometheus/Grafana users on Unraid cannot graph tool latency or error rates.
what: `/metrics` (Prometheus text) with run counts, durations, errors, install times, queue depth; optional OpenTelemetry export with run ids as spans.

title: Multi-instance and HA story
why: The design is one process, one SQLite file, one lib volume; running two replicas behind a proxy would split state.
what: Document single-instance as the supported topology; optionally support PostgreSQL via a thin DB adapter and shared object storage for caches for users who need replicas.

title: n8n integration
why: David runs n8n; n8n's MCP Client node and HTTP Request node are the natural way to chain OmniForge tools into workflows, and n8n webhooks are the natural trigger source.
what: Make the server consumable by n8n's MCP Client node (needs R-09), publish an n8n workflow template that calls `tools/call`, and let F-08 webhooks accept n8n's payloads; document a round trip (n8n cron -> OmniForge tool -> n8n notification).

title: Run context for scripts
why: A script cannot know which tool it is, which client called it, or a run id to correlate its own logs.
what: Inject `OMNIFORGE_TOOL`, `OMNIFORGE_RUN_ID`, `OMNIFORGE_CALLER` env vars and a tiny optional helper (`omniforge.log()`, `omniforge.progress()`) available on the path.

title: Progress notifications and cancellation
why: Long scrapers run silently up to the timeout; MCP supports `progressToken` and `notifications/cancelled` but the transport cannot send server-to-client messages.
what: With R-09's SSE channel, forward script progress lines (A-09) as progress notifications and honour cancellation by killing the process group (R-06).

title: Per-tool network policy
why: Once isolation exists, 'network off' is binary; a lottery tool should reach `national-lottery.co.uk` and nothing else.
what: Per-tool egress allowlist (hosts/CIDRs) enforced via the sandbox's network namespace and a small forwarding proxy; default deny for new tools when enabled.
